title: Which step changes where the trick ends?
description: The trick is changed so it ends on three, then on five, by changing the number that is added. A longer trick with multiply by three, add twelve and divide by three is then followed with a letter and checked with seven. Keeko doubts that we add three to end on three.
teaching_notes: One idea: follow the letter through every step and see which step fixes the ending. Watch for students who add the wanted ending itself, forgetting that the division by two halves it.

source: Change the trick so it always ends on 3, then on 5. Then che
video_script.why: A child sees that the added number decides the ending, and that a letter shows where any longer trick ends.
video_script.substitution: the book's own trick with the added number changed, then a longer trick followed with the letter ex
video_script.anchor: the trick card: double, add a number, divide by two, take away the start
video_script.wrong_answer: we add three to end on three
video_script.wrong_move: adds the wanted ending itself, and forgets that dividing by two halves it
video_script.payoff_line: Adding six ends on three, adding ten ends on five, and the longer trick ends on four.

final_answer.spoken: add six, add ten, and the longer trick ends on four

hold_back: the longer trick always ends on 4
maths_rules: Add 6: 2x + 6, then (2x + 6) / 2 = x + 3, then x + 3 - x = 3.
Longer trick: 3x, then 3x + 12, then (3x + 12) / 3 = x + 4, then x + 4 - x = 4.
Doubt: start 5, 10, then 10 + 3 = 13, then 13 / 2 = 6.5, then 6.5 - 5 = 1.5, which is not 3.
video_script.design: One idea: the added number is the step that fixes the ending. The trick card stays in the anchor band and each letter line sits on the working board.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book. It asks us to change the think of a number trick.
<bookmark mark='trick'/>The old trick doubles the number, adds four, divides by two, and takes away the start.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can you change one step so that the trick ends on three, and then on five?

beats.on_screen: the trick card holds still and the words end on 3, then on 5? glow

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a pair card: add 4 gives the end 2; the number being added is circled

marks.pair: the pair card add 4, end 2 appears
marks.change: the number 4 in the card is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='pair'/>In the old trick the number added was four, and the end was two.
<bookmark mark='change'/>We change the number that is added, and watch the end.

beats.on_screen: Given: double, add a number, divide by 2, subtract the start; longer trick: multiply by 3, add 12, divide by 3, subtract the start

marks.long: the longer trick is written under it

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the old trick is double, add a number, divide by two, and take away the start.
<bookmark mark='long'/>The longer trick is multiply by three, add twelve, divide by three, and take away the start.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number to add for an end of 3 and of 5; where the longer trick ends

marks.find: the things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number to add for an end of three and of five. We also find where the longer trick ends.

beats.on_screen: start x: 2x; add 6: 2x + 6; divide by 2: x + 3; subtract x: x + 3 - x = 3
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step one, add six instead of four, so two ex becomes two ex plus six.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Divide by two to get ex plus three. Both parts are halved.
<bookmark mark='end'/>Taking away ex leaves three, so adding six gives an end of three.

beats.on_screen: start x: 2x; add 10: 2x + 10; divide by 2: x + 5; subtract x: x + 5 - x = 5
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, add ten, so two ex becomes two ex plus ten.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Divide by two to get ex plus five.
<bookmark mark='end'/>Taking away ex leaves five, so adding ten gives an end of five.

beats.on_screen: longer trick, start x: x × 3 = 3x; 3x + 12; (3x + 12) ÷ 3 = x + 4; x + 4 - x = 4
narration: <bookmark mark='triple'/>Step three, the longer trick starts with ex and multiplies by three to get three ex.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add twelve to get three ex plus twelve, and divide by three to get ex plus four.
<bookmark mark='end'/>Taking away ex leaves four, whatever the start is.
<bookmark mark='triple'/>Step four, check with seven. Seven times three is twenty one, and twenty one plus twelve is thirty three.
<bookmark mark='end'/>Thirty three divided by three is eleven, and eleven take away seven leaves four.

beats.on_screen: Answer: adding 6 ends on 3, adding 10 ends on 5, and the longer trick ends on 4
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Adding six ends on three, adding ten ends on five, and the longer trick ends on four.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: add 3 for an end of 3; a test with 5: 10, 13, 6.5, 1.5 is written; 1.5 sits next to the wanted 3; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble add 3 for an end of 3 appears
marks.strike: 1.5 sits next to the wanted 3 and the bubble is struck out

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we add three to end on three.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Test it with five. Double it to get ten, and add three to get thirteen. Halve it to get six and a half.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Taking away five leaves one and a half, not three, because the halving cut the three in half.
